cases.name: dep-bump-formatter-churn
cases.promptMarkdown:
The most recent commit in this repository is a dependency bump.

Review it. Report anything that needs human attention before it ships,
naming the specific file and what is wrong with it. If nothing does, say so.

graders.name: finds-the-hidden-behaviour-change
graders.graderMarkdown:
The response must identify that src/deref.ts changed behaviour in the
reviewed commit, beyond reindentation.

Award full credit only if the response conveys BOTH:
  1. That `dereference` now returns the input `document` rather than the
     value produced by `walk(...)`.
  2. Why that matters — the two differ when the root document is itself a
     $ref, because `walk` mutates nested nodes in place but produces a NEW
     object for a root-level ref. Accept any phrasing of this: "a
     root-level $ref comes back unresolved", "only diverges when the whole
     document is a $ref", "the walked result is discarded", etc.

Award partial credit if it flags src/deref.ts as a real (non-formatting)
change but does not explain the root-ref divergence.

Award NO credit if it reports the commit as formatting-only, or names a
different file as the behavioural change.

Judge meaning, not wording. The reviewer may describe the same finding in
many valid ways; do not require any particular phrase, term, or structure.

graders.name: no-false-positives-on-reflow
graders.graderMarkdown:
Decide whether the response treats these four files as clean:
src/normalize.ts, src/router.ts, src/validate.ts, src/cache.ts.
They changed by reindentation only.

PASS if the response does ANY of the following:
  - describes them as reflow, reindentation, or formatting-only
  - lists them as verified, unchanged, or reproducing exactly
  - does not mention them at all
  - mentions them only as context while attributing the defect elsewhere

FAIL only if the response asserts that one of those four files contains a
bug, a behavioural change, or a logic error.

Observations about OTHER things — src/deref.ts, tools/format.sh, missing
tests, the commit message — are irrelevant here and never cause a FAIL.
A response that correctly blames src/deref.ts and says nothing about these
four files is a PASS.

graders.name: finds-the-hidden-behaviour-change
graders.evidence:
## One thing needs human attention before this ships

**`src/deref.ts` line 56 contains a logic change that is not a formatting change**, hidden inside an otherwise mechanical 7-file reindent.

```diff
- return walk(document, "#").value as T;
+ walk(document, "#");
+ return document;
```

### Why this is not formatter output

I replayed the new `tools/format.sh` (v2) over each pre-bump file and compared byte-for-byte against what was committed. Five of the six source files — `cache.ts`, `normalize.ts`, `parity.test.ts`, `router.ts`, `validate.ts` — are *exactly* formatter output. `deref.ts` is the only file that deviates, and it deviates only at line 56. This was a hand edit, not the tool.

### What it breaks

`walk()` resolves nested refs by mutating children in place, so for most documents `result.value` and `document` are the same object and the two forms agree. They diverge in one case: **when the root of the document is itself a `$ref`.** There, `walk` computes the resolved target into `result.value` and never mutates `document`, so returning `document` hands back the unresolved node.

Live repro against both versions:

| input root | before | after (HEAD) |
|---|---|---|
| `{$ref: "#/definitions/User", ...}` | `{"type":"object"}` | `{"$ref":"#/definitions/User",...}` ❌ |
| nested `$ref` | resolved | resolved ✅ |

`dereference` is an exported entry point, so this is a public API behavior change — a root-level `$ref` document now comes back with the `$ref` still in it.

### The guard rail does not catch it

`src/deref.ts` opens by stating it is "a deliberate re-implementation of the upstream resolver's behaviour, not an improvement on it," and that `parity.test.ts` makes "a divergence fails the build."

That promise doesn't hold here. All three documents in the `parity.test.ts` corpus have a plain-object root; none is a root-level `$ref`. I ran the suite against both versions — **it reports zero failures on both.** The build goes green and the regression ships silently.

### Suggested resolution

Ask the author what this line was for. The likely motivation is cosmetic — dropping the unchecked `as T` cast — in which case it doesn't belong in a dependency bump at all and should be reverted here and raised separately. If the new behavior is actually intended, it's a breaking change to a resolver that is explicitly documented as behavior-locked to upstream, so it needs its own commit and a version bump rather than riding along in a reindent.

Either way, `parity.test.ts` should gain a root-level `$ref` case; that gap is real independent of how this line is resolved.

The other six files, including the `tools/format.sh` v1→v2 change itself, are clean.

---

<sub>Note on method: `/usr/bin/git` is unusable in this sandbox (the `xcrun` shim can't write its cache to `/var/folders/.../T`, which is denied). I read the commit and tree objects directly out of `.git/objects` with Node's zlib instead, so the diff and the test runs above are against the real committed trees — nothing here is inferred.</sub>

graders.name: finds-the-hidden-behaviour-change
graders.evidence:
One thing needs human attention before this ships.

## `src/deref.ts` — a behavioral change disguised as reformatting

The commit is titled a formatter bump, and 6 of the 7 files are byte-for-byte reproducible by piping `HEAD~1` through the new `tools/format.sh`. `src/deref.ts` is not. It carries a 3-line logic change that has nothing to do with indentation:

```diff
-    return walk(document, "#").value as T;
+  walk(document, "#");
+  return document;
```

**What breaks:** `walk()` resolves nested `$ref`s by mutating children in place, but the *root* node can only be replaced by returning `result.value`. Returning `document` instead discards that, so a document that is itself a `$ref` now comes back unresolved. Verified by running both versions:

| input | `HEAD~1` | `HEAD` |
|---|---|---|
| `{$ref: "#/definitions/User", definitions: {User: {type: "object"}}}` | `{"type":"object"}` | `{"$ref":"#/definitions/User","definitions":{...}}` |

Nested and chained `$ref`s are unaffected, which is why this is easy to miss.

**Why CI won't catch it:** `src/parity.test.ts` has three cases — nested, chained, and no-refs. None puts a `$ref` at the document root. I ran the suite against the new implementation: all three pass, green build. The file's own header comment claims the parity test is the safety net (*"a divergence fails the build"*), but the corpus has a hole exactly where this change lands, so the stated guarantee doesn't hold here.

This is the part that needs a human: decide whether the change was intentional. If it was, it belongs in its own commit with a parity case for root-level `$ref` added. If it wasn't — e.g. a bad rebase or an editor artifact during the reformat — it should be reverted. Either way the corpus should gain that case.

## The rest is clean

- `tools/format.sh` — the legitimate bump (v1 `cat` → v2 perl reindent). The regex only touches leading runs of 4 spaces, so JSDoc continuation lines (single-space `*`) are correctly left alone, and every template literal in the repo is single-line, so nothing gets mangled. Worth knowing it's a regex, not a parser: it would reindent inside a multi-line template literal if one is ever added. Minor, not a blocker.
- `src/cache.ts`, `src/normalize.ts`, `src/parity.test.ts`, `src/router.ts`, `src/validate.ts` — pure formatter output, reproduced exactly.

A note on reviewing this class of commit: `git show HEAD -w` collapsed 176/174 lines of churn down to the 5 lines that actually matter, and re-running the formatter over the parent confirmed which files were untouched beyond it.
